subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Atlantic hurricane season and the Eastern Pacific hurricane season are two regional systems tracked by meteorologists.
• Both seasons officially last six months.
• The peak activity months of the two seasons don't align.
• The peak month of the Atlantic season, September, falls during the fourth month of the Eastern Pacific season, which begins in mid-May.
• The peak month of the Eastern Pacific season, August, falls during the third month of the Atlantic season, which begins in June.
prompt: The student wants to emphasize a difference between the Atlantic and Eastern Pacific hurricane seasons. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Tracked by meteorologists, the Atlantic hurricane season lasts six months and has its peak activity in September.
choices.B: The Eastern Pacific hurricane season begins in mid-May, and its peak month is August.
choices.C: The peak activity months of the two seasons don't align; for example, the peak month of the Atlantic season falls during the fourth month of the Eastern Pacific season.
choices.D: The Atlantic hurricane season and the Eastern Pacific hurricane season, both tracked by meteorologists, each officially last six months.

explanation:
Choice C is the best answer. The sentence emphasizes a difference between the Atlantic and Eastern Pacific hurricane seasons, directly stating that the peak activity months don't align and providing a concrete example: the peak month of the Atlantic season falls during the fourth month of the Eastern Pacific season.

Why D is incorrect:

Choice D is incorrect. While the sentence mentions both seasons, it emphasizes that both officially last six months—a similarity between them, not a difference.
